title: Every USB Port Color Explained (White, Black, Blue & More)
description: USB port colors are not a design choice. Each one tells you the speed and the era of the port. In this video we go through every color, one by one.
hook_say: You have probably seen a blue USB port sitting right next to a black one and assumed the colors were just a design choice. They are not. Every color means something, and once you know what, you will stop plugging things into the wrong port.
thumb_image: a row of colorful USB-A ports: white, black, blue, red, on a metal computer panel

chapters.name: White USB ports
chapters.label: WHITE
chapters.icon: a single white USB-A port on a metal computer case panel, front view
chapters.hook: White USB ports are the ones nobody talks about, and they were the first ones ever made.

beats.say: White ports are USB 1.0 and 1.1 from 1996, and they were the first ones ever made.
beats.image: two white USB-A ports stacked on the back panel of an old beige desktop computer

beats.say: If you have ever seen a white USB port, you were looking at a genuinely old computer.
Before USB, plugging anything into a computer was a mess. Your printer had one type of port, your mouse a different one, your keyboard something else again.
beats.image: an old beige inkjet printer from the 1990s
beats.label: Printer
beats.image2: a beige ball mouse with a round PS/2 connector
beats.image3: a beige mechanical keyboard from the 1990s with a large DIN plug

beats.say: Speed wise, white ports could move about one and a half megabytes per second. A single photo from your phone today is around five megabytes. So this port would need about three seconds just to move one picture.
beats.label: USB 1.1 top speed
beats.image: a modern smartphone lying on a table showing a photo gallery

beats.say: White ports vanished once USB 2.0 arrived, but USB 1.1 never fully died. Car stereos, budget speakers and basic MP3 players still use it. Why pay for a faster chip when the slow one does the job?
beats.show: Why pay for a faster chip?
beats.image: a car stereo head unit with a USB port on the front
beats.label: Car stereo
beats.image2: a small black portable MP3 player with a tiny screen

chapters.name: Black USB ports
chapters.label: BLACK
chapters.icon: a single black USB-A port on a metal computer case panel, front view
chapters.hook: Black is the USB port you have plugged into a thousand times, and it has a speed ceiling you probably hit every day.

beats.say: Black is USB 2.0, released in the year 2000, and for a decade it was the port on everything.
beats.image: a black USB-A port on the side of a silver laptop

beats.say: It moves data at up to 60 megabytes per second, forty times faster than white.
beats.label: USB 2.0 top speed

beats.say: That is fast enough for a keyboard, a mouse, a printer, or a webcam. Which is exactly why they are still everywhere.
Where it hurts is big files. Copying a full movie takes minutes, not seconds. If your external drive feels slow, check the color of the port first.
beats.image: an external hard drive connected by cable to a laptop

outro.say: Next time you plug something in, look at the color first. Subscribe, because next Monday we take apart something else you use every day.
outro.show: Look at the color first. See you next Monday.
